title: Daily camera-trap detections of 15 carnivore species at 1,340 sites in northern California forests, 2009-2018 (one to three years per site)
creator: Furnas, Brett J.; Goldstein, Benjamin R.; Figura, Peter J.
citation: Furnas, B. J., Goldstein, B. R., & Figura, P. (2021). Intermediate fire severity diversity promotes richness of forest carnivores in California [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.6078/D1DT4S
abstract: Daily detection/non-detection of 15 mammalian carnivores from camera traps at 1,340 sites across northern California forests, surveyed between early August and early December in 2009-2018 for up to 30 days, with day of year, climate, vegetation and fire severity / pyrodiversity covariates per site-year and site-year coordinates coarsened to 0.1 degree.
samplingProtocol: Paired camera traps per hexagon surveyed concurrently for 2-5 weeks between early August and early December each year; all mammal detections identified to species; detection per species per 24-hour survey day, up to 30 days.
closureNote: closed within a site's annual survey (up to 30 days), open between years; 111 sites were surveyed in more than one year
geographicCoverage: Northern California forests, USA (about 38.2-42.0 N, 120-124 W)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: site coordinates (deposited to about 8 decimal places) coarsened to the 0.1 degree cell centre with coarsen_coords(): fisher (southern Sierra Nevada DPS) and Sierra Nevada red fox (DPS) are listed as endangered under the US Endangered Species Act; a precaution, as no species is IUCN CR/EN/VU

notShipped.lag: the authors' previous-day detection term, a function of y
notShipped.project: a 0/1 per site-year flag the deposit does not define
notShipped.exact_coordinates: site coordinates finer than 0.1 degree (E7 precaution)

notes: Coordinates differ between years at 72 revisited sites and are given per site-year (period_). Covariates are per site-year as the authors computed them (period_). Day of year is deposited for all 30 days; y is NA on days the camera was not operating, so a site-year's surveyed days need not be consecutive. Two survey days carry a day of year above 365 and so fall in the following January.
